In [[mathematics]], a '''Zassenhaus group''', named after [[Hans Zassenhaus]], is a certain sort of [[doubly transitive permutation group]] very closely related to rank-1 [[groups of Lie type]].

== Definition ==

A '''Zassenhaus group''' is a permutation group ''G'' on a finite set ''X'' with the following three properties:

* ''G'' is doubly transitive.
*Non-trivial elements of ''G'' fix at most two points.
*''G'' has no regular [[normal subgroup]]. ("Regular" means that non-trivial elements do not fix any points of ''X''; compare [[free action]].)

The '''degree''' of a Zassenhaus group is the number of elements of ''X''.

Some authors omit the third condition that ''G'' has no regular normal subgroup. This 
condition is put in to eliminate some "degenerate" cases. The extra examples one gets by omitting it are either [[Frobenius group]]s or certain groups of degree 2<sup>''p''</sup> and order
2<sup>''p''</sup>(2<sup>''p''</sup>&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)''p'' for a prime ''p'', that are generated by all [[semilinear map]]pings and Galois automorphisms of a field of order 2<sup>''p''</sup>.

== Examples ==

We let ''q'' = ''p<sup>f</sup>'' be a power of a prime ''p'', and write ''F<sub>q</sub>'' for the [[finite field]] of order ''q''. [[Michio Suzuki (mathematician)|Michio Suzuki]] proved that any Zassenhaus group is of one of the following four types:

* The [[projective special linear group]] PSL<sub>2</sub>(''F''<sub>''q''</sub>) for ''q'' > 3 odd, acting on the ''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 points of the projective line. It has order (''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)''q''(''q''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)/2.
*The [[projective general linear group]] PGL<sub>2</sub>(''F''<sub>''q''</sub>) for ''q'' > 3. It has order (''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)''q''(''q''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1).
*A certain group containing PSL<sub>2</sub>(''F''<sub>''q''</sub>) with [[Index of a subgroup|index]] 2, for ''q'' an odd square. It has order (''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)''q''(''q''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1).
*The [[Suzuki–Ree group|Suzuki group]] Suz(''F''<sub>''q''</sub>) for ''q'' a power of 2 that is at least 8 and not a square. The order is (''q''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)''q''<sup>2</sup>(''q''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)

The degree of these groups is ''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 in the first three cases, ''q''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 in the last case.
